newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hogs called steady-up $0.50 - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hogs called steady-up $0.50 - trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices were called steady to $0.50 per cwt higher Thursday, with frigid cold expected to slow marketings and force higher bids from meat packers, livestock sources said.
"If it wasn't for the weather, we would be lower," said an Indiana dealer, who was expecting singe-digit Fahrenheit temperatures Thursday morning.
The Indiana source said hog marketings swelled Wednesday as farmers sold hogs before the cold arrived.
The cold arrived Wednesday in the western Midwest where sub-zero temperatures occurred in western Iowa and Nebraska.

One meatpacker buyer in that area said a lack of hogs caused slaughter at one plant to be reduced 40 percent Wednesday. USDA estimated Wednesday's total U.S. hog slaughter at 328,000 head, versus 354,000 a week ago and 369,000 a year ago.
Low tempereatures Thursday morning were forecast to range from three degrees below zero F in northwest Iowa to nine above in Indiana.
